clue.text: Supports a parent but doesn't talk about it

definitions.meaning: to provide for one's mother is literally to keep Mum
the idiom '...' means stays silent about something

explanation.surface: Someone quietly pays for an elderly parent's upkeep and never mentions it.
explanation.walkthrough: MUM is the British word for mother; 'keep mum' is a British idiom for staying quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings are the same phrase: providing for a mother, and the idiom for keeping a secret.

clue.text: Make use of unfinished polymer plastic

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the remaining letters are reshaped into a new order
unfinished says the word polymer loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone decides to put a half-made batch of polymer plastic to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the R of polymer, leaving POLYME; 'plastic' rearranges those letters. 'Plastic' looks like a noun after polymer but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something to use is a direct synonym for hiring or utilising it.

clue.text: Simple sort of medieval song?

definitions.meaning: plainsong is the unaccompanied chant of the medieval church, so this word names that sort

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works as the first half of 'plainsong', medieval church chant; the question mark admits it is only part of the term.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple and unadorned are synonyms; plainsong is a kind of early church music named with this word.

clue.text: Comic often aims to make political statement

indicators.note: comic means funny or absurd, so the following letters are jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A comedian's habit of aiming jokes produces something like a party's declaration of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' looks like a noun for a comedian but signals rearranging OFTEN AIMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A party publishes a manifesto as its public declaration of policy and aims.

clue.text: Members of Italian society breaking the rules

definitions.text: Members of Italian society breaking the rules

parts.words: Members of Italian society breaking the rules
parts.note: a cryptic description of members of the Sicilian criminal brotherhood, a lawbreaking 'society' from Italy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Society' suggests polite company, but the society meant is the Sicilian criminal organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is an Italian criminal organisation whose members are lawbreakers by definition.

clue.text: Jack found among big shots, very rich men

indicators.note: found among says the sailor's letters sit inside the word for big shots

parts.note: nobs are important or upper-class people
a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor turns up among the important people, a set of extremely wealthy men.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is a traditional name for a sailor, and AB stands for able-bodied seaman; nobs is British slang for posh people.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabobs were Britons who returned from India with great fortunes, hence wealthy men generally.

clue.text: Mean to get a girl

parts.note: the mean or average is the norm

explanation.surface: Someone sets out, perhaps unkindly, to win a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective for unkind but is the noun for an average.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female forename, so it stands for a girl in crossword convention.

clue.text: See man on board crushing endless grain

indicators.note: crushing here says the chess piece presses down on the grain, placing it first

parts.note: a bishop is a chess piece, a man on the board

indicators.note: endless says the grain loses its final letter

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: Look: a fellow on deck is grinding down an unfinished cereal crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushing' puts the chess piece on top in this down light. 'See' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese, and 'man on board' a sailor but is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is his diocese, the area under a bishop's authority.

clue.text: Had inspiration?

parts.note: inspiration is literally drawing air into the lungs, so having it means drawing air in

explanation.walkthrough: Inspiration suggests a creative idea; the literal sense is inhaling.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration in the physiological sense is inhaling, so to have had it is to have taken in air.

clue.text: Odds on wet weather causing injury

indicators.note: on means placed next to, with the betting letters coming before the weather

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's odds on a rainy day lead to someone getting hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is a racing term for a horse's final odds.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is an injury to a ligament, typically from twisting a joint.

clue.text: Quartet heard and observed as anticipated

indicators.note: heard says the number word for a quartet is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a quartet is four
observed means seen

explanation.surface: A singing group of four was listened to and watched, just as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns FOUR into its sound-alike FORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foreseen was predicted in advance, the same as being anticipated.

clue.text: A Ford not moving forward — then back!

indicators.note: moving means set in motion, so the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A Ford car that won't go forward, only into reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not moving' reads as a stalled car, but 'not' is part of the letters and 'moving' alone signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes motion one way and then the other, back and forth.

clue.text: Assumes parking will be limited by migrating toads

indicators.note: being limited by means being enclosed on either side by the other letters
migrating means moving elsewhere, so the letters of toads change position

parts.note: P is the standard map abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Parking spaces get restricted while toads cross the road on their migration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'migrating' rearranges TOADS to ADOTS, and P goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a manner or position is to assume or take it on.

clue.text: They raise the spirits

parts.note: cheering people up is the surface; the cryptic reading is places that produce whisky and gin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise the spirits' means cheer up, but here spirits are alcoholic drinks, made in quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilleries are works that manufacture alcoholic spirits such as whisky.

clue.text: Not unique type of bridge

definitions.meaning: a copy matching another is not one of a kind
a competitive form of the card game where every table plays the same deals

explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is the card game, not a river crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy is not one of a kind; in competition card play, identical deals are replayed at each table.

clue.text: Queen's favourite isle? Crete possibly

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Was the Queen's favourite island perhaps Crete?
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was the favourite of Elizabeth I; 'isle? Crete' suggests a Mediterranean holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl of Leicester was Elizabeth I's famous courtier and favourite.

clue.text: A death sentence impending or just some bird?

definitions.meaning: British judges once donned a black square of cloth before passing sentence of death
a small warbler with a dark crown

explanation.walkthrough: In British courts a judge put on a black cap to pronounce a death sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The judge's sombre headwear signalled execution; the same name belongs to a common European warbler.

clue.text: He can't help helping himself

parts.note: helping himself means stealing, done compulsively

explanation.walkthrough: 'helping himself' sounds like self-reliance but means taking things, and 'can't help' signals compulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with this disorder feels an irresistible urge to steal.

clue.text: Publicity coverage for speech

parts.note: an ad is publicity
a dress covers the body

explanation.surface: A press officer seeks media coverage for a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coverage' looks like media reporting but means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk given to an audience.

clue.text: Not a Mr mistaken as Mrs?

definitions.note: a married woman's title stands for a married woman

indicators.note: mistaken means got wrong, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A woman is not a Mister, and is wrongly called Missus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistaken' rearranges NOT A MR; the whole clue suggests a woman wrongly addressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A matron is a married woman, especially a dignified one, the person titled Mrs.

clue.text: Lively turn I have put on

indicators.note: put on says the first piece is placed before the second

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: An energetic music-hall number I have staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' suggests staging a show but works as the joining signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Active and lively are synonyms for energetic.

clue.text: Be sent up to bed, having gone into a decline

indicators.note: sent up says in this down light the word Be is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone is sent off to bed after falling ill and fading.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light, 'sent up' means read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide ebbs when it falls back, so the word means declined or receded.

clue.text: Approached wanderer uneasily

indicators.note: uneasily means not settled, so the letters are unsettled into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: To have drawn near is to have come closer, a synonym of approached.

clue.text: Bwana's new title?

indicators.note: new says the letters are made over in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Has the African master been given a new honorific?
explanation.walkthrough: Bwana is a Swahili term of respect, 'master'; rearranged it gives an Indian honorific.
explanation.definitionFit: A nawab was a Muslim governor in Mughal India, later an honorary title of rank.

clue.text: Make message unintelligible in mad rush

definitions.meaning: to encode a signal so that it cannot be read

explanation.walkthrough: One verb sense covers coding a message; one noun sense covers a frantic dash.
explanation.definitionFit: Encoding a signal jumbles it; a frantic scramble is a hurried, disorderly rush.

clue.text: Check rower's seat

definitions.meaning: to check is to block or frustrate
the crosswise bench in a boat where an oarsman sits

explanation.walkthrough: The verb means to frustrate; the noun is a boat's crossbench.
explanation.definitionFit: To frustrate a plan is to check it; the same word names a rowing boat's crosswise bench.

clue.text: Add a very quiet finale

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
a finale is an end

explanation.surface: Add a pianissimo closing section to the music.
explanation.walkthrough: PP (pianissimo) is the musical marking for very soft.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to attach or add something at the end.

clue.text: Dance orchestra with woman leader

parts.note: Sara is a woman's name, and as leader she comes first
a band is a group of musicians, an orchestra

explanation.surface: A dance band with a female leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like the conductor but puts SARA first.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarabande is a slow, stately Spanish dance in triple time.
